primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria due to an acquired PIGA-mutant hematopoietic clone
mechanism: A somatic PIGA mutation in a hematopoietic stem cell impairs glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchor biosynthesis, causing loss of GPI-anchored complement regulators such as CD55 and CD59 and thereby permitting complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis and thrombosis.
vignette: A 31-year-old man has episodic dark urine, fatigue, and an unprovoked hepatic-vein thrombosis. Laboratory studies show Coombs-negative intravascular hemolysis. Flow cytometry demonstrates a population of erythrocytes and granulocytes that lack both CD55 and CD59.
lead: Which of the following molecular abnormalities most directly explains these findings?
correct: A somatic PIGA mutation that prevents normal glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchor biosynthesis
distractors: An inherited CD55 mutation that selectively prevents decay of C3 convertase
A germline factor H mutation causing uncontrolled alternative-complement activation
A spectrin mutation causing loss of erythrocyte membrane surface area
Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency causing impaired NADPH production
distractor_notes: An isolated inherited CD55 defect would not explain loss of multiple unrelated GPI-anchored proteins such as both CD55 and CD59 across a clonal population of blood cells.
Factor H defects cause complement dysregulation such as atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome; they do not cause the acquired GPI-anchor deficiency characteristic of PNH.
Spectrin defects cause hereditary spherocytosis with membrane instability and extravascular hemolysis, not acquired loss of CD55/CD59.
G6PD deficiency causes oxidant-triggered hemolysis through impaired red-cell antioxidant defense, not loss of GPI-anchored complement regulators.
key_expl: PIGA is required for synthesis of the GPI anchor that tethers many proteins to the cell surface. A somatic PIGA mutation in a hematopoietic stem-cell clone causes deficiency of GPI-anchored proteins, including the complement regulators CD55 and CD59. Loss of these regulators makes blood cells vulnerable to complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis and contributes to thrombosis.
objective: Explain PNH as an acquired somatic PIGA defect causing loss of GPI-anchored CD55/CD59 and complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis.
clues: clonal loss of CD55 and CD59
